The only attached picture is declared as an actual frame at 0ms, and frame_preservation requires that the entire composite sheet — the top hero shot, the three middle turnaround panels, the four bottom detail close-ups, and all of the existing panel lettering (HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, BOOTS) — remain the whole supplied frame at that instant, never cropped down to just the hero figure. So the shot keeps the full sheet composition and animates within it: rain streaks falling and wet-ground reflections shifting in the hero panel, faint life in the studio-lit detail panels, under one slow, gentle push-in that drifts the framing without removing the panel layout or the labels. No cut is needed for a five-second drifting animation, so a single continuous take is used. The user asked for no speech, no singing and no added visible text, so those classes stay off; music is permitted under balanced creativity but is not requested, so it is not marked requested. No replacement of any figure is requested, so the replacement map stays empty.

shots.action: The full vertical character reference sheet fills the frame exactly as supplied, its three tiers intact: at the top the wide hero panel with the black-clad tactical figure standing upright, arms at the sides, head turned toward the viewer's left on a rain-slick industrial walkway between dark metal railings, distant city lights and lit windows glowing behind him; across the middle the three equal full-body turnaround panels of FRONT, SIDE PROFILE and BACK against the plain dark gray studio backdrop; across the bottom the four detail close-ups of FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS and BOOTS. The entire sheet drifts toward the viewer in one slow, barely perceptible push, the figure's weight settling a hair as his coat hem and collar edges stir in the damp air, but no panel ever crops away, reorders or loses its lettering.
